title: Request deduplication tombstone reconciliation mismatch causing sporadic undercount
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Observed intermittent undercount of token-metering events for a small subset of customers. Symptoms are reproducible in internal staging with crafted retries and simulated shard failovers. Root cause appears to be a mismatch between the request-level deduplication tombstone lifecycle and the downstream rollup/reconciliation semantics across shard boundaries. The bug results in lost increments in daily rollups (under-reported usage), causing billing differences and inaccurate per-route SLO metering.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a tenant route with short client retry TTL and enable cross-shard failover in staging
2) Send a request with an idempotency key that triggers a long-running generation and intentionally simulate a network retry from the client (send same idempotency key from a different edge shard),
3) Force a shard handoff / migration while the request is inflight (simulate lease revocation),
4) Observe two ingestion events: one from the original shard and one from the retrying shard; both write meter increments with the same request id metadata but different shard annotations

5) Run daily rollup/reconciliation; verify the deployed reconciler deduplicates only within-shard and then applies compact/compensating-logic that inadvertently drops one of the increments leading to undercount in the final aggregate
impact:
- Intermittent under-reporting of usage (observed in ~0.03% of sampled requests in staging load tests).
- Affects per-route and per-credential daily rollups and therefore invoices for a small number of customers.
- Can mask noisy retries and obscure root cause analysis for rate-limits and SLA investigations.
root_cause: The deduplication system stores tombstones keyed by client idempotency token and shard_id to keep dedupe checks cheap. During shard handoff, a retry from a different shard will bypass the local tombstone check and create a duplicate increment. The downstream rollup/reconciler performs de-duplication with a heuristic that expects cross-shard duplicates to be merged by a later compaction job; however, the compactor uses an expiration window that can evict the older duplicate before compaction runs. Additionally, the compaction only retains one increment but incorrectly attributes it to the wrong route under certain ordering, causing the reconciler's compensating adjustments to drop the other increment rather than merge them. In short: mismatched dedupe key scoping (per-shard) + compactor TTL ordering race -> lost increments in final rollup.
proposed_fixes: 1) Make deduplication keys globally routable: include a stable global dedupe namespace so retries routed to other shards still hit dedupe entries (short-term config flag to enable on staging),

2) Update rollup/reconciler to deduplicate on a global request_id fingerprint (not shard-scoped) and make compactor idempotent: ensure compaction merges increments deterministically and never drops unique event counts,
3) Extend compactor retention window by +15 minutes to avoid eviction-before-merge race while we audit performance impact,
4) Add integration test that simulates cross-shard retry + lease handoff and asserts final daily totals are consistent with canonical source-of-truth (in-memory golden),
5) Run a controlled canary enabling the global-dedupe flag for low-risk customers and compare reported usage against previous baseline for 48h before wider rollout
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests updated: dedupe keying unit tests for global namespace and shard-scoped fallback pass
Integration test added: cross-shard retry + handoff does not change final aggregated totals in staged end-to-end test
Compactor retention change validated in staging with no regressions on storage and compaction latency
Canary 48h comparison shows no statistically significant undercount for canary tenants
PR reviewed and merged with at least two approvers from infra/metering teams
Documentation updated: dedupe semantics and compaction guarantees section in metering runbook
notes: This bug manifests only under a confluence of events (long running request + client retry + shard handoff + compactor timing). It is low-frequency but high-cost when it hits billed customers. We should prioritize a defensive fix (global dedupe keying + compactor idempotency) before large scale shard resharding planned in Q2.
